title: Taking the Train
subtitle: On Sunday Emma takes the train downtown. It is late.
description: An A1 reading and listening text about getting around an American city by train: tickets, stops, and being late.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: On Sunday I take the train downtown. I want to see my friend Anna.
The station is ten minutes from my apartment. I buy a ticket for three dollars.
The train is late. I wait on the platform for fifteen minutes. It is cold, and I am not happy.
Then the train comes. It is full, and I don't get a seat. I stand for four stops.
At the fifth stop a man gets off and I sit down. Outside the window I see the lake. The water is gray today.
I get off downtown at ten past two. Anna is in front of the station with two coffees.

exercises.title: Understanding the Text
exercises.instructions: Read again and choose the best answer.

items.explanation: “I want to see my friend Anna.”

items.prompt: How long does Emma wait on the platform?
items.explanation: Fifteen minutes is a quarter of an hour.

items.prompt: Why does Emma stand on the train?
options: Because there are no free seats
Because it is a short trip
Because she wants to see the lake
items.explanation: “It is full, and I don't get a seat.”

options: When a man leaves the train
items.explanation: “At the fifth stop a man gets off and I sit down.”
“Anna is in front of the station with two coffees.”

items.prompt: Is Anna angry that Emma is late?

exercises.title: Make the Sentence
exercises.instructions: Put the words in the correct order.

items.prompt: Say when you leave the train.

items.statement: The train comes at the right time.
Emma has a seat for the whole trip.
items.explanation: False. She stands for four stops.

items.statement: Emma can see water from the train.
items.explanation: True. “Outside the window I see the lake.”
True. She is waiting “with two coffees”.

discussion: How do you go to work or to school?
Is it far? How long does it take?
Do you take the bus or the train?
Are the buses and trains late where you live?
